claims.text: The hotel is at 15 Place Vendôme, 75001 Paris.

findings.quote: its principal place of business (the Ritz Paris Hotel) at 15, Place Vendôme, 75001 Paris, France

claims.text: In 2012 the hotel closed for the first time in its history and reopened four years later with updated technologies and new facilities.

findings.quote: in 2012, the hotel closed for the first time in its history, re-emerging four years later with updated technologies, new facilities

claims.text: A grand staircase winds up from the lobby.

findings.quote: The majestic grand staircase still winds its way up from the lobby

claims.text: Higher-floor rooms and most suites have balconies or terraces.

findings.quote: higher floor rooms and most suites have balconies or terraces

claims.text: Rooms have signature details such as key-shaped light switches and silk tulip lampshades.

findings.quote: signature flourishes like key-shaped light switches and silk tulip lampshades

claims.text: Bar Vendôme is a glass-ceilinged brasserie that serves a Japanese breakfast in the morning.

findings.quote: the glass-ceilinged Bar Vendôme brasserie (try the Japanese breakfast in the morning)

claims.text: Afternoon tea with madeleines is served in the Salon Proust.

findings.quote: the Salon Proust for a decadent afternoon tea replete with perfectly spongy Madeleines

claims.text: The Ritz Bar, launched in September 2021, is a lantern-topped space serving cocktails inspired by astrological signs.

findings.quote: Launched in September 2021, the Ritz Bar is a dramatic, lantern-topped space serving glamorous cocktails
that are inspired by astrological signs

claims.text: The hotel has a pool and a central garden.

findings.quote: a dip in the shimmering pool, and a quiet drink in the lush central garden

claims.text: Treatments include La Prairie facials and massages with French-made oils formulated specially for Ritz Paris.

findings.quote: facial treatments using La Prairie or massages featuring French-made oils formulated specially for Ritz Paris

claims.text: There is a David Mallett hair salon, a nail bar and a makeup area, plus a shopping arcade with luxury boutiques and a Ritz concept store.

findings.quote: There’s also a David Mallett hair salon, a nail bar, and a special area for makeup
The shopping arcade houses luxury boutiques and a Ritz concept store.

claims.text: Wi-Fi is complimentary.

findings.quote: Wi-Fi is complimentary

claims.text: Swiss hotelier César Ritz partnered with French chef Auguste Escoffier to open the hotel in 1898.

findings.quote: In 1898, Swiss hotelier César Ritz partnered with French chef Auguste Escoffier to open

claims.text: Coco Chanel lived at the hotel for 34 years and has a suite named for her; Ernest Hemingway, another regular, gives his name to both a suite and a bar.

findings.quote: Coco Chanel; the latter, who lived here for 34 years, has a suite named for her, while fellow regular Ernest Hemingway’s name adorns both a suite and (what else?) a bar

claims.text: Guests can book a class at the Ecole Ritz Escoffier cooking school, which also offers classes for kids.

findings.quote: book a class at the L'Ecole Ritz Escoffier cooking school to up your kitchen game (kids' classes are also offered)

claims.text: The marble bathrooms keep peach-colored robes and towels, a hue chosen by Mr. Ritz, and golden swan bathtub taps.

findings.quote: fluffy, peach-colored robes and towels (a hue personally chosen by Mr. Ritz), and golden swan bathtub taps
The marble bathrooms have been refreshed and modernized

claims.text: All rooms have marble fireplaces, and the design of each Prestige Suite aims to reflect its namesake, with antique books lining the Marcel Proust suite.

findings.quote: All rooms have marble fireplaces
The design of each of the Prestige Suites aims to reflect their respective namesakes, so you’ll find antique books lining the Marcel Proust space

claims.text: Most rooms have no coffee or tea making facilities, so coffee and tea are ordered from room service.

findings.quote: How about room service: Worth it?
you'll need to order coffee and tea, as there are no facilities for making them in most of the rooms

claims.text: WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's palace status.
